subject: E-Commerce
title: Counterfeit Goods at the Border
description: A micro-lesson that makes Counterfeit Goods at the Border usable.

hook.text: Customs seized $3 billion in counterfeit goods in 2023. Cross-border e-commerce is the primary channel for fakes.

buildup.text: Online marketplaces make it easy to sell counterfeits. Fake Nike shoes, replica handbags, & knockoff electronics flood.

discovery.text: Customs agencies use AI image recognition to compare product photos with known counterfeits in shipment X-rays.

twist.text: Many buyers knowingly buy counterfeits. A $20 'Gucci' bag from AliExpress has its own market of willing customers.

climax.text: Counterfeits cost legitimate brands $500 billion annually. Cross-border e-commerce is the superhighway for fakes.

punchline.text: $3B seized, $500B lost to fakes. The same pipes move goods move counterfeits.

quiz.question: How do customs agencies detect counterfeit goods in cross-border shipments?
options: AI image recognition comparing shipment X-rays with known counterfeit patterns
